findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the dish machine to be testing at 0 PPM CL. Discussed with PIC. Until new sanitizer is used, use triple sink to wash, rinse, and sanitize the dishes. Inspector will return 02/24/2025 to re-asses violations.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 1) Kitchen manager handled cell phone to call PIC upon arrival of inspector and did not wash hands prior to returning to work. Kitchen manager proceeded directly to the walk-in cooler and removed a tub of food after hanging up the phone.  
2) Server was observed entering the kitchen to prepare to go orders and did not wash hands prior to scooping rice and handling plastic utensils. Plasticware was handled by food contact surface due to storage practice. 
Handwashing between tasks was discussed. PIC was asked to revisit this with all staff.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the kitchen and engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Kitchen manager was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to drying hands. PIC discussed and demonstrated proper technique with kitchen manager. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the kitchen handwashing sink. Paper towel dispenser was jammed. Rolls of paper towels were placed by the kitchen handwashing sink. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) 1) Portion of snow peas stacked in a pan on the top right side of a prep cooler were observed at 54F. Peas were said to be stored in the cooler overnight. Peas were discarded.
2) Shell eggs on the top left side of a prep cooler were observed with surface and internal temperatures at 60F-64F. PIC confirmed with kitchen staff the eggs were placed out on the cookline next to the wok prior to inspector’s arrival. Eggs were placed in the cooler when staff saw inspector. Eggs were to be used or discarded by the end of lunch service. 
Best practices for storage of TCS foods in the tops of prep coolers and time control were discussed.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: The walk-in cooler was observed to not have items date marked. Ensure date marking is accomplished to ensure the integrity of the food is not compromised. This involves a 7 day life expectancy of the food items where the day of creation/preparation marks day one. For example, if food is prepared on a Sunday, that is day one. Therefore, Saturday would be day 7 and the food item is to be discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: Shrimp was observed to be thawing in a 5 gallon bucket of non-running water on the prep table. This bucket of shrimp was moved to the triple sink and a steady stream of running water was placed over the bucket to allow the shrimp to be fully submerged under the running water. Ensure this practice continues in the future for any meat item that is being thawed.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.comment:
3-304.12: The handles in the dry ingredient storage bins were observed to half be stored correctly while the other half were stored with their handles making contact with the ingredients. This behavior was corrected for the half that were stored incorrectly. Ensure this practice continues to reduce the risk of contamination from hands in the raw ingredients.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed walk-in cooler fan to have ice build-up. Ice on vent was melting and allowing water to spray out into the walk-in cooler area. Uncovered foods are contacting contaminated water. Cover foods and ensure cooler is in proper repair. Reference 3-304.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed can opener to be heavily soiled. Observed ice scoop to be in contact with soiled container. Ensure food contact surfaces are clean and not in contact with soiled surfaces. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Observed the scoop for rice stored incorrectly in stagnate, room-temperature water . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Employees were eating lunch when inspector arrived and entered the kitchen, did not wash hands, and began handling foods in the kitchen. No hand washing was observed during the inspection and there was no soap available at the hand washing sink at the beginning of the inspection (See Violation below). Hand washing was discussed. Hand washing must occur upon entering the kitchen, between tasks, and before putting on gloves to name a few times when hand washing must occur.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Food employee entered kitchen and handled food without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: No soap was available at the hand washing sink in the kitchen at the beginning of the inspection and the paper towel dispenser was having difficulty dispensing. A very small amount of liquid soap was taken from the wait station hand sink to the kitchen hand sink upon request. Hand washing sinks must always be supplied with soap and paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed the deli slicer in the kitchen to be soiled with raw beef and raw chicken. Deli slicer needs detailed cleaning on the knobs and all surfaces. Scrub, wash, rinse and sanitize deli slicer.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Cooked chicken in the walk in cooler is probed at 50F and 59F. This is the tub of in-use chicken through the lunch period that was placed back in the walk in cooler approximately 1/2 hour ago. Time as a control was discussed--once time and temperature control for safety foods are removed from their temperature control/cooler, they may only be used for up to 4 hours and then must be discarded (up to 6 hours if chicken remains at 70F or below). This may mean pulling smaller amounts at a time and leaving the rest in a cooler. Chicken was removed between 11 and 12 and will be discarded by 5:30 pm.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135°F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
A common towel is observed on top of vegetables in the walk in cooler. Do not use common towels or linens in direct contact with food. 

Food is observed stored in t-shirt bags in the back reach in freezer. Do not store foods in t-shirt bags--always make sure containers are food grade.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.13  (C) Linens are in direct contact with food. Linens may not be used in contact with food. Reference 3-304.13.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Rice scoop observed stored in water in between use. Store scoops clean and dry. 

Knives in the kitchen are stored in between metal shelving and containers sitting on the shelves. This area is not easily cleanable and knives should not be stored in between this area.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: The handle to one of the in use knives in this kitchen is broken and there are unnecessary crevices on the handle that are no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Replace this knife.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces have rusted or are no longer easily cleanable. Replace with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a food service facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: a) the wire shelves in the walk in cooler are soiled with dripping grease and dust accumulation, b) the handles to all cold holding units are soiled with build up, c) the surfaces of stools, buckets, racks, shelving in the kitchen are soiled with grease and food build up. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors under the cook line equipment are soiled black with grease accumulation. Floors need to be cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed a tub of chicken in the walk in cooler that was probed at an internal temperature of 55F and shell eggs that were 54F. It appears as though these items are being pulled for use during busy periods and held at room temperature and then being cooled down after the rush. Maintain cold foods at 41F or below at all times. This is the same for the egg roll items that were stored above pans in the top of the prep cooler. Air flow circulates from the bottom and these will not be maintained at 41F without proper refrigeration. These items were all cooled rapidly to 41F or below as they were reported to have been out for less than 2 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: 1) Observed beans and tofu in the walk in cooler that were not covered. Many items were observed being covered at the time of the inspection. 2) Observed raw beef in the reach in freezer in the back to be stored directly in a grey Wal-Mart shopping bag. Beef was voluntarily discarded and it was discussed to store foods in food grade containers.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed three knives stored in a soiled container at the end of the cook line. Knives and container were taken to the dish area to be washed, rinsed and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed a package of raw chicken stored in the walk in cooler on a top shelf above ready to eat foods such as vegetables and noodles. Chicken was moved to the bottom rack where the rest of the chicken was stored. Store ready to eat foods above raw meats to protect from contamination. 3-302.11  (P) Store ready to eat foods above raw meats to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed a container of cooked pork and a container of a cooked sausage stored in a pan that was sitting on top of the containers in the top of the prep cooler. Pork and sausage were probed with a recently calibrated digital thermometer at an internal temperature of 63F. It was discussed that these should be discarded and in the future, foods such as carrots or asparagus may be stored in this pan, but all time and temperature control for safety foods must be stored where the refrigerated air is able to keep them at 41F or below. 2) Observed cooked chicken in the walk in cooler that was probed at 63F. This chicken was reported to have been cold, taken from the walk in cooler to use through lunch near the fryers, and then placed back in the walk in after lunch service. This is abusing the temperature of the food. Pull only what you need at that time and keep the rest of the chicken temperature controlled until use (or place on a time as a control policy as discussed). These items were to be voluntarily discarded. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed the condenser unit in the walk in cooler to be dripping onto the floor right in front of the food storage shelves. Repair walk in condenser unit so that if it drips, the water is not contaminating the food stored below.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.12  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. Reference 3-305.12.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 1) Observed a bowl being used as a scoop and stored within a container of crushed peanuts. Do not use bowls as scoops--use a scoop with a handle and store extended up and out of the food. 2) Observed rice scoop being stored in water in between use. Store rice scoop clean and dry or within rice as long as the handle is always stored extended up and out of the food.  Observed 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 1) Observed the microwave in the kitchen to show signs of rust along the interior frame when door is open. 2) Observed the top of the chest freezer to be heavily damaged with an accumulation of rust visible. Repair or replace these items so that non-food contact surfaces are smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable. 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces have rusted or are no longer easily cleanable. Replace or repair equipment  with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a food service facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 1) Observed the outsides of some of the bulk containers, lids of containers, handles of containers, and handles of coolers to be soiled with food debris and grease accumulation. 2) Observed old date marking labels to not have been removed from working containers of food in the prep cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently and remove old date labels after use. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: Observed a couple of sweatshirts/jackets stored on the dry storage shelves intermingled with packaged food. Store employee clothing in designated areas away from food. 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed bulk sauces in the walk in cooler that were not date marked with the date of preparation, an open gallon of milk in the reach in cooler that was not date marked, and sauces at room temperature both on the wok line and individually portioned. All ready to eat, time and temperature controlled for safety foods (or house made sauces) must be date marked with the date of preparation and held refrigerated at 41F or below for a maximum of 7 days. Sauces are reported to be made every 2 days and were date marked during the inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed flats of shell eggs stored above a box of cabbage in the walk in cooler. Cabbage was moved during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed ketchup stored in an open can in the walk in cooler. Acidic foods when opened from a can must be transferred into a food grade container that is labeled and not left in an open can.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed cups being used as scoops and stored within the food in the sauces in the walk in cooler and in the containers of flour, etc. Only use scoops with handles and store the handle extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Dish machine tested at 0 ppm bleach sanitizer. Facility was aware that the sanitizer was not dispensing and had placed a call to GFS yesterday, but was continuing to use the dish machine without any other intervention. The three compartment sink was set up during the inspection (instructions on how to prepare 3 compartment sink were provided) and facility was instructed that all dish was must go through the entire wash, rinse and sanitize process. That means they may either manually wash, rinse and sanitizer OR use the dish machine to wash and rinse and transfer to the three compartment sink to sanitize until dish machine is repaired.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket at the wait station tested at 0 ppm and it appeared as though there might be soap in this bucket as well. Sanitizer buckets should contain a bleach solution only prepared to 100 ppm on test strip. Do not put soap in with the sanitizer as soap must be rinsed off before using sanitizer.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the ice flap in the ice machine with black friable mold, 2) the ice scoop holder next to the dish machine with pink slime, 3) the can opener blade with food debris accumulation. Wash, rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom of the two door reach in freezer in the back to be soiled with food spillage. Clean this freezer.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
No soap was available at the wait station hand sink at the beginning of the inspection. Soap was provided during the inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed two bottles of chemicals underneath the three compartment sink and a couple bottles of chemicals at the wait station to not be labeled with the common name of the contents. Label all chemicals removed from their original container. Bottles were labeled during the inspection. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed personal beverages stored on a prep surface right next to clean dish ware for the public. Store personal beverages with a lid and straw in an area below or away from food or dish ware for the public, ideally near the hand sink so hands can be washed after touching the beverage. Personal beverages were moved during the inspection.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the upright freezer in the kitchen to have a significant accumulation of ice on the shelves. Defrost freezer. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
Observed old date labels on in use dish ware. One container of chicken had date labels from 8/22 and 8/26 on it but chicken inside was reported to be from the batch that was made on 9/3 that is in the walk in cooler. Old date labels were observed on several containers throughout the facility. Remove old date labels after each use and make sure containers are being washed, rinsed and sanitized in between use.
750-830f Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a chemical spray bottle with what was reported to be degreaser in it at the end of the wok line that was not labeled with the name of the contents. Bottle was labeled during the inspection. Make sure all chemical spray bottles are labeled with the name of the contents.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed sauces prepared in the facility to be stored at room temperature. Sauces are on the wok line, at the egg roll area, and stored in large 5 gallon buckets at the back of the kitchen. It was discussed that since these items are made on site, they must be treated as potentially hazardous and be marked with the date of preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum. Only pull the amount for the wok line that you will go through in 4 hours and discard any left at the end of 4 hours. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
Observed an employee use his bare hands to garnish a dish with sprouts. Avoid bare hand contact with ready to eat foods. Gloves must be worn or tongs or another sort of barrier used.
750-280 Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop in the sugar to not have a handle. Make sure all scoops have handles and store them with the handle extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a cardboard box being used as a table/drawer at the egg roll station. Cease the use of cardboard and replace with something smooth and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths being stored on prep surfaces. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use or make sure they find their way to the soiled linen after use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to be soiled with an accumulation of debris. Wash, rinse and sanitize can opener.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a container of medication to be stored in a cardboard box with utensils used in the facility. Medications must be stored in areas separate and away from any food or food equipment.
750-1330 Personal medications shall not be stored in food storage, preparation, or service areas. Properly store personal medications.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed noodles in the four door reach in cooler with no date mark. PIC stated they were prepared on Saturday(12/24). Noodles were date marked to CORRECT the violation.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed straws stored at the front hand sink with no protection. Cover straws to provide protection and prevent possible contamination.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed multiple wet wiping cloths on various prep surfaces. Store wet wiping cloths in a sanitizer bucket in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed personal items such as tums, tylenol, and hats stored in various places in the kitchen. Store personal belongings in a designated area away from food.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No employee with their FSSMC was present during the inspection.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in the chest freezer. Provide thermometer.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed eggs stored above peppers and lettuce in the walk in cooler. Eggs were moved to the bottom shelf to CORRECT the violation.  2) Observed straws stored underneath the soap and paper towel dispenser at the hand sink. straws were immediately moved to CORRECT the violation.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed multiple items in the walk in cooler with no protection. All items were covered to CORRECT the violation.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed tums and lense cleaner stored on a shelf at the cook line. Personal items should be stored in a segregated area awat from food preparation. Items were immediately moved to CORRECT the violation.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1)Observed multiple wet wiping cloths on various prep surfaces. Wet wiping cloths should be stored in a sanitizer bucket in between use. 2) Observed soap being combined with bleach in a sanitizer bucket. Sanitizer buckets should not be mixed with soap as this messes with the concentration of the sanitizer.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) The ice deflector of the ice machine was soiled with what appears to be mold. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces. 2) The can opener was soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service utensils at the front prep area(forks, knives, spoons, etc) stored in multiple directions. Store utensils with their food contact surfaces all facing in the same direction to prevent possible cross contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed a sauce stored in a can of oyster sauce. Single service containers should not be re-used. Replace with a food grade container.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the wait station hand sink. Provide paper towels.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
1) Observed multiple items in the walk in cooler with no date mark. Cooking dates were discussed with the cook. Food items were properly date marked to CORRECT the violation. 2) Observed chicken in the walk in cooler at 50F. Cook stated the chicken had started cooling at nine. A time stamp should be provided. Food should cool down to 70F within two hours and 41F or lower within an additional four hours.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed clean forks with their food contact surface side up stored underneath the dripping soap dispenser. Wash, rinse, and sanitize forks. Store forks in a protected area/Store food contact surface side down.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
1) Observed broccoli in the walk in cooler with no protection. Provide protection. 2) Observed soup hot holding on the prep counter with no protection. A lid was provided to CORRECT the violation.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the white rice utensil laying in the rice. Store in-use utensil with the handle extending out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed multiple wet wiping cloths throughout the facility. Store wet wiping cloths in a sanitizer bucket in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Can opener was soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surface. 2) The microwave was soiled with food splash. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surface. 3) The ice deflector on the ice machine was soiled with what appears to be mold. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surface.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed blood splash on the bottom of the turbo air freezer at the back of the facility. Clean non food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed single service spoons stored in multiple directions. Store utensils in the same direction to prevent contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed food debris on the small bowls used for rice. Rice bowls were stored with their food contact surface side up. Store bowls with their food contact surface side down.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The mop sink was separating from the wall. Reseal sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
